chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a female slave of a people who went to a tribe other than her own and informed them that she was free, 'I am free.' A man from them married her and she bore him children. He said: Her children are enslaved unless she establishes proof that two witnesses testified for her that she is free; then they are not enslaved and they become free.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the children of a female slave who claims to be free and marries?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the principle of 'al-walad li-l-firash' (children follow the status of the mother) in the context of a slave woman's claim of freedom. It highlights the evidentiary standard required to overturn the presumption of slavery, noting that while the default is enslavement, the testimony of two witnesses confirming her free status liberates her offspring. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on verifying lineage and status through credible testimony to determine the child's legal standing.
